source_name: Kosovo Banking Association (Shoqata e Bankave të Kosovës) — Events archive
why_relevant: The association's event archive is the single richest weak-signal channel for the cell: forums, workshops and conferences co-attended by BQK and the FIU. Observed items include a 'Payments Forum 2025 — Digital Payments Ecosystem in Kosovo', an Inter-Institutional AML/CFT Workshop 2025-2026, instant-payments workshops and a Corporate & Retail Banking Strategies conference scheduled 27-29 October 2026. Event titles reveal the rule areas banks are being prepared for.

source_name: Kosovo Banking Association — Trainings catalogue (Trajnimet)
why_relevant: Training catalogue certified by ATTF/House of Training Luxembourg, delivered with the association's AML/CFT Committee. A new compliance course appearing in the catalogue is a leading indicator that a corresponding supervisory requirement is landing. Course descriptions name the committees and expert bodies involved.

source_name: Kosovo Banking Association — Partners / Important Links page
why_relevant: Association link hubs typically enumerate regulators, donor programmes and training partners (ATTF/House of Training, member banks). Ideal snowball seed for expanding the actor map of this cell.

source_name: BQK — Trainings and Seminars (Currency in Circulation)
why_relevant: A regulator-run training page. Courses are aimed at banks, MFIs and insurers; the training curriculum tracks the operational requirements BQK intends to enforce (cash handling, counterfeit detection). Low-volume but a genuine regulator-side training calendar.

source_name: IFC / SECO — Partnership with Central Bank of Kosovo to Advance Digital Financial Services
why_relevant: Donor-project artefact that names the rule under preparation before it exists: IFC with Swiss SECO supporting BQK on a draft law on payment services and open banking, explicitly to create a supportive regulatory environment. This is exactly the pre-legislative signal the cell targets, and IFC/SECO publish project updates and sometimes deliverables.

source_name: GIZ — Improving financial governance in Kosovo (project page)
why_relevant: GIZ project pages state objectives, partners, budget and end dates — a donor timetable that often precedes institutional reform. Scope observed is public financial governance (accountability, transparency, effectiveness) rather than bank supervision, so relevance to A3 is partial but worth a low-frequency watch; GIZ Kosovo's country portfolio page is the pointer to any newer financial-sector project.

source_name: Deutsche Bundesbank — EU-funded ESCB programme for Western Balkans central banks / banking supervisors (Kosovo beneficiary)
why_relevant: Programme announcements and closing events describe exactly which supervisory capabilities BQK was being built up in — banking supervision, financial stability, consumer protection, NPL resolution, payment systems, legislative alignment. That component list is a forward map of Kosovo's supervisory agenda. Bundesbank is the consortium lead and publishes launch/closing press releases with named deliverables.

source_name: Agencija za bankarstvo Republike Srpske — Programme of support to central banks and banking supervisors (sr-language coverage of the same ESCB/IPA programme)
why_relevant: Serbian-language description of the same EU/ESCB regional programme in which Kosovo's central bank is a beneficiary. Peer beneficiaries publish more component and timetable detail than BQK does, so this is a lateral read-across for what Kosovo is receiving. Also supplies the Serbian-language terminology set (supervizija, program podrške) for further sr searching.

source_name: European Commission DG NEAR — Kosovo financial assistance under IPA (project fiches & programming documents)
why_relevant: IPA project fiches and action documents are terms-of-reference-grade artefacts: they state the regulatory deliverable, the beneficiary institution and the timetable years before the rule. A 2008 Kosovo project fiche is already exposed on this domain, indicating the document type is published here. Best single pointer for donor-funded regulatory work in Kosovo.

source_name: EEAS — EU Projects with Kosovo
why_relevant: EU Office in Kosovo project listing — the local-delegation view of ongoing technical assistance, including launch events and calls. Complements the DG NEAR programming layer with implementation-stage announcements.

source_name: Office of the Prime Minister — Programi për Reforma në Ekonomi (Economic Reform Programme, ERP)
why_relevant: The ERP is an annually updated commitment document negotiated with the European Commission; its financial-sector chapter pre-announces planned laws and regulations with target years. Not a legal act, so it never appears in regulation searches — a classic indirect artefact for this cell.

source_name: ARKEP — Agjenda Digjitale e Kosovës 2030 (Kosovo Digital Agenda)
why_relevant: Strategy document naming digital-finance and e-payment objectives and the donors backing them (GIZ, World Bank, USAID, SIDA and others are listed as ICT-sector donors). Strategy annexes typically carry an action plan with responsible institutions and deadlines — pre-legislative timetable material touching payments.

source_name: EBRD — Kosovo Country Strategy (Albanian edition)
why_relevant: IFI country strategies state intended policy-dialogue and technical-cooperation priorities for the financial sector over a multi-year horizon — i.e. which regulatory reforms an IFI intends to push and fund. Published in Albanian, which also yields local regulatory vocabulary.

source_name: World Bank — Kosovo Financial Sector Strengthening Project (documents & reports)
why_relevant: Project appraisal and implementation documents specify regulatory and supervisory deliverables agreed with BQK, with disbursement-linked timetables. Later implementation-status reports report slippage — an early signal of delayed rules. World Bank documents portal is fully crawlable and versioned.

source_name: Balkan Payment Forum (ProMoney Events) — agenda and speaker list
why_relevant: Regional commercial conference (14 May 2026, Tirana) whose published agenda names the regulatory topics the region is preparing for — PSD3 impact, first six months of SEPA live, cashless-adoption incentives, KYC/KYB and fraud — and lists Kosovo-based speakers (e.g. the founder/chairman of Pysera Kosovo) alongside central bankers. Speaker lists are a cheap actor map of who is driving payments regulation locally.

source_name: Payments/fintech event calendars (The Paypers, paytech.events, FintechNews CH)
why_relevant: Aggregated conference calendars are efficient pointers for discovering regional events where Kosovo regulators and banks appear; from a calendar entry one snowballs to the agenda and speaker list, which is where the substance sits.

source_name: Center of Excellence in Finance (CEF), Ljubljana — regional capacity-building institute (Kosovo member state)
why_relevant: CEF supports capacity development for finance officials across SEE with Kosovo among its 12 member constituencies, covering central-banking reform alongside PFM and tax. Its learning programme is a regulator-facing training calendar; a new CEF course line for Kosovo officials indicates a reform direction. Note: the specific training-calendar URL was not confirmed in this run — only the institution and Kosovo's membership were.

source_name: CBCG (Central Bank of Montenegro) — EU projects page (twinning precedent template)
why_relevant: Peer central bank that publishes its full twinning/technical-cooperation inventory, including the IPA 2014 'Support to Regulation of Financial Services' twinning with Bundesbank, HNB, DNB, BaFin and HANFA. Useful as a template for what a Western Balkans twinning in financial-services regulation contains and which EU institutions staff it — the same consortium actors recur for Kosovo.

source_name: Kosovo Banking Association — LinkedIn and Facebook pages
why_relevant: Practical workaround for the 403-defended association website: event announcements, workshop photos naming BQK and FIU officials, and training promos are mirrored on social channels, often earlier than on the site. Also the discovery channel for events that never get a web page.

source_name: Albanian-language financial media event coverage (Telegrafi, KosovaPress, Ekonomia.info, BotaSot, Lajmi.net)
why_relevant: For conferences and workshops with no published agenda, Albanian-language media is the only record: they report the theme, the officials present and the statements made about forthcoming rules. Observed covering both the BQK/IMF crypto conference and Banking Association milestones. Cross-outlet duplication also allows corroboration.

source_name: AmCham Kosovo — chamber news and committee activity
why_relevant: Business chambers run sector committees and host policy panels where draft rules are debated with regulators before publication; AmCham Kosovo publishes statements and operates in three languages (en/sq/sr). Relevance to the financial-services workstream was NOT confirmed in this run — no financial-sector panel was found — so this is a speculative but cheap watch. The Kosovo Chamber of Commerce (oek-kcc.org) is the local-language counterpart with a publications section.

source_name: GZK — Consolidated Acts view (Aktet e konsoliduara)
why_relevant: Dedicated sub-view of the gazette portal listing acts in consolidated (amended-to-date) form. This is the cheapest way to know whether a banking/payments law currently in circulation as a PDF is superseded, and by which amending law.

source_name: GZK — Laws in force list (Lista e ligjeve në fuqi)
why_relevant: Authoritative in-force/not-in-force determination. Distinguishes repealed banking law (04/L-093) from the new Law No. 08/L-304 on Banks published Jan 2026 — exactly the kind of supersession A3 deadline tracking depends on.

source_name: Konsultimet — consultation list endpoint (Lista e konsultimeve)
why_relevant: Machine-friendly listing with institution/status/date filters; the concrete surface to poll for open comment windows and their closing dates. Confirmed reachable by fetch (page last-updated stamp 26.08.2026, EU-funded).

source_name: Konsultimet — consultative meetings register (Takimet konsultative)
why_relevant: Consultation is not only written: the platform separately registers consultative meetings, which often carry earlier, unpublished-elsewhere signals on a draft financial act and dates by which stakeholders must respond.

source_name: Konsultimet — reports and documents (Raportet e konsultimit)
why_relevant: After a consultation closes, line ministries must publish a report stating which comments were accepted or rejected and why. This is the closest thing Kosovo has to a 'feedback statement' and is the retrospective record of what a withdrawn or altered draft rule used to say.

source_name: Konsultimet — statistics dashboard
why_relevant: Aggregate counts per institution reveal which ministries actually consult and at what cadence — a proxy for whether a financial-sector rule change will be visible in advance or arrive unannounced.
